newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil plans April GDR, convertibles presentation.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil plans April GDR, convertibles presentation.

text.p: Russia's biggest oil company LUKoil will present its planned global depositary receipt (GDR) programme and a new issue of convertible bonds in London on April 29, a senior company official said on Monday.

Vice-President Leonid Fedun told a briefing the convertible bonds would be issued through a consortium of three Western investment banks -- Natwest, SBC Warburg and Paribas -- and Russian financial adviser NIKoil.

LUKoil made two issues of convertible bonds in 1995, which were mainly bought up by Atlantic Richfield Co (ARCO), a U.S. oil company, which as a result ended up with 7.99 percent of LUKoil. The two companies also have a $5 billion joint venture.
Fedun did not say how big the GDR programme or bond issue wouuld be.
"The board of directors has decided to raise around 4.5 trillion roubles, most of which will come through the global placement," he said.
Fedun said in December LUKoil planned to raise at least $1 billion through a global issue of shares this year.

LUKoil is also working on plans to issue level-three American Depositary Receipts on its ordinary shares, he said. It already has accounts audited to international standards for 1994 and 1995, and will have 1996 GAAP accounts in the middle of this year.
The U.S. authorities require foreign companies issuing level-three ADRs, which raise capital and are equivalent to a share listing, are required to present three years of audited accounts.
LUKoil was one of the first Russian companies to issue level-one ADRs, which allow investors to trade shares of a non-U.S. company without domestic settlement problems.
It has also announced plans for ADRs on its preferred shares this year, but Fedun did not say how these plans were progressing.
